evidence.note: Up front reads every dev test/helper, names the task a 'massive undertaking' and commits to 'build this efficiently' — framing effort allocation against the full graded surface rather than diving into one corner.

Builds the entire function catalog breadth-first (math, stats, distributions, financial, date, engineering, database, lookup, text, dynamic arrays) and all endpoint families before any deep edge-case work — securing broad working coverage first.

Explicitly reasons about the hidden suite: 'the verifier has more comprehensive grading. Let me look at corner cases I might have missed', 'Hidden tests on text functions - my modern text functions are basic', and defers items judged 'probably not tested' (sheet rename with cross-sheet refs) — conscious return-weighted triage.

Consciously declines to invest in REST->WS broadcast after reasoning 'all tests use WebSocket directly, not REST. So my current setup is OK' — deliberately NOT over-investing in a likely-ungraded path.

Latter half is a stream of targeted depth probes on high-risk areas (spill shrink/# syntax, iterative calc cycles, date-format mm context, 1000-cell perf), each checked against likelihood of being graded — depth timeboxed to plausibly high-yield spots.

reasoning: The agent clearly matches the level-8 anchor: it explicitly reasons about graded return, secures broad working coverage across the entire function catalog and endpoint families before deep edge-case work, and consciously defers low-yield niches ('probably not tested', REST->WS 'OK'). It shows some level-10 traits (risk-based depth probing, weighing marginal coverage) but the allocation is a stream of ad-hoc 'let me also check' probes rather than a deliberate, revisited allocation ledger with explicit reallocation, so it falls short of 10.
